_comment: FAST Driver Intelligence Database
Two independent signals are stored here:
1. Gaming-stability recommendation (per vendor > gpu_family > game):
recommended    - the driver version FAST actively recommends for competitive gaming
latest_tested  - newest driver the FAST team has bench-verified. MAY be newer than
recommended - that gap is the whole point of the feature, and the
card says so out loud ('newer, but not our pick')
latest_known   - newest driver the VENDOR has actually released. Moves whenever the
driver-watch routine sees a new release; latest_tested only moves
when someone benches it. latest_known >= latest_tested always.
The gap between them is what lets the card say 'X is out, we have
not measured it' instead of staying silent about a driver it has
never heard of. Optional - absent, it collapses to latest_tested
and the card says nothing, which is the pre-2026-07-31 behaviour.
fallback       - { version, why } the driver to drop back to when the recommended one
misbehaves on a specific rig. Must be older than recommended
avoid          - list of driver versions with known gaming regressions
notes          - measured evidence for the recommended version and the fault for each
avoid version. See WRITING A NOTE below
download_url   - direct link to the recommended driver download page
WRITING A NOTE - a note is EVIDENCE ONLY. It is never the verdict.
DriverIntelligence.cs owns the verdict, the headline and the instruction, because those
depend on which of the six states the user is in and the same note is reused across
more than one of them. A note that says 'avoid this driver' or 'FAST's pick' will read
as nonsense in the other state that renders it.
Write the note as a sentence fragment that completes both of these:
Good verdict   -> 'Why it is our pick: <note>'
Update verdict -> 'What you gain: <note>'
Avoid verdict  -> 'The fault: <note>'
The Hold verdict (added 2026-08-20, and now the DEFAULT - see the Recommendation policy
section of hardware-reference.md) renders NO note. It fires when the user is at or above
`recommended` and something newer exists that we have not measured, so there is by
definition no evidence to show. Its copy is entirely hardcoded. Do not add a note keyed
to latest_known hoping it will surface there - it will not.
So start lower-case and lead with the consequence to the user, not with what the driver
is. Not 'Game Ready Driver (2026-05-26), major branch jump' but 'your FPS drops the
longer you play'. Measured numbers second. Cap at 2-3 sentences.
Do not repeat what the same page already shows: install steps belong to the Driver Update
Flow stepper, the voltage cap has its own card, and the release date is in the driver-age
line. Full bench data goes in hardware-reference.md, not in the note.
ONLY TWO KINDS OF NOTE EXIST HERE - do not add a third:
- notes[recommended]   shown to users already on it and, via the Update verdict, to
everyone on an older driver
- notes[<avoid entry>] shown to users sitting on a known-bad driver
Every other version is unreachable by design: anything newer than latest_tested gets
hardcoded 'newer than tested' text, and any other older version renders notes[recommended].
46 such entries were deleted on 2026-07-31 - they were prose no user could ever see. Do
not re-add per-version changelog entries. Version history belongs in hardware-reference.md.
fallback deliberately has NO note - its one-line 'why' lives in the field itself.
2. Security advisories (top-level security_advisories block):
Curated from NVIDIA PSIRT (github.com/NVIDIA/product-security) and AMD Product
Security. Each entry is a single vendor security bulletin that may bundle multiple
CVEs. FAST flags an advisory as unpatched when the user's installed driver is
OLDER than fixed_in_version. Newer driver branches are assumed to forward-port
the fix (NVIDIA's standard practice). The signal is separate from the gaming
recommendation - a user on the gaming-recommended driver may still see a
security warning if they are behind on bulletins, and vice versa.
GPU family matching is done by substring against the detected GPU name.
Example: 'RTX 40' matches 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070', 'RTX 4090', etc.
Driver versions use the short NVIDIA format (e.g. '595.97') or AMD format (e.g. '26.3.1').
NVIDIA versions are converted from WMI format (32.0.15.9597 -> 595.97) at detection time.
PUBLISHING - this file ships ONLY with the app. There is no out-of-band channel.
It is an embedded resource. DriverIntelligence.LoadDatabase reads it from the
assembly and from nowhere else. Editing it reaches users when the change is merged
and a release goes out - the same way every other change reaches them.
DO NOT BUILD A FETCH-FROM-fast-updates UPDATER FOR THIS FILE. That has been built
and deleted once already (added 9dfa7cb 2026-07-31, removed e93eedb 2026-08-05),
and this note is what was left describing it afterwards - which is how it came to
be rebuilt a second time on 2026-08-27 before the history was checked. Read e93eedb
before proposing it a third time. Its argument, still true when re-checked on
- Releases ship far faster than this file changes. v9.0.0 through v9.1.2 was four
releases in six days; this file changes every 1-3 weeks. The embedded copy is
therefore never meaningfully stale, and the gap is covered by an update the
user is already offered on launch.
- The delivery path never delivered anything. Its publish workflow failed every
run on a missing FAST_UPDATES_TOKEN, nothing was ever published, and nobody
noticed for five days - because the app degrades silently to the embedded copy.
- It costs a credential to rotate and a monitor to watch, to duplicate a delivery
path that is already faster.
The premise to re-test before reviving it is the release cadence, not the plumbing.
If releases ever slow to less often than this file changes, the trade flips.
The weekly driver-watch routine refreshes the gaming notes, the security advisories
block, and latest_known from upstream vendor sources.
Severity is the highest CVSS v3.1 base score across the bundled CVEs in the bulletin.
FAST flags 'unpatched' when installed driver version < fixed_in_version.
GeForce / Windows scope only - vGPU, Linux, Tesla, datacenter bulletins are excluded.
Cross-vendor reference: NVIDIA PSIRT at github.com/NVIDIA/product-security.

nvidia.title: GPU Display Driver - January 2026
nvidia.summary: Kernel-mode driver flaws (use-after-free, integer overflow) in nvlddmkm.sys plus a NULL-pointer dereference in the HD Audio driver. Local low-privilege attacker could escalate to code execution, data tampering, or denial of service.

nvidia.title: GPU Display Driver - October 2025
nvidia.summary: Multiple kernel-mode driver vulnerabilities affecting GeForce on Windows. Local privilege escalation, code execution, and information disclosure.

nvidia.title: GPU Display Driver - July 2025
nvidia.summary: Twelve CVEs covering kernel-mode driver and user-mode component issues. Local attacker could achieve code execution and privilege escalation.

nvidia.title: GPU Display Driver - January 2025
nvidia.summary: Seven CVEs in the kernel-mode display driver. Local privilege escalation and information disclosure.

fortnite.latest_known_reports: Several users, mostly on RTX 50 cards, report the screen freezing or going black for a few seconds, usually while a video plays in Chrome or Edge, and say it stops after going back to 617.42; a few also report S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 stuck on a black screen at launch. NVIDIA is collecting crash data but has not listed either as a known issue.

fallback.why: the last driver before the 610 branch jump

notes.610.47: on a 4080 SUPER it improved frame-time consistency by 38%, and on a 2080 Ti it removed the hard stalls entirely (min FPS 2.1 to 22.7, 1% lows +21%, stutter time -28%). It does shift burst-moment work onto the CPU, so a CPU older than a 9900K or Ryzen 5000 can bottleneck in heavy scenes.
notes.610.74: your screen flickers to black and comes back, at the desktop as well as in game. It is this release specifically, not the whole 610 branch.

fortnite.latest_known_reports: Nothing yet in the field. AMD lists these itself: on Windows 10 installing it can switch Smart Access Memory off, so check it is still on afterwards; games can crash or time out when another overlay such as Xbox Game Bar opens or closes while AMD's Performance Metrics Overlay is on; on RX 9000 cards using FSR Frame Generation, switching apps can crash or hang the PC; and on RX 7000 cards Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and Valor Mortis can crash or time out.

notes.26.3.1: no known Fortnite regressions on RDNA 4, plus FSR 4.1. Not bench-tested by FAST - this pick tracks AMD's known-issues list, not our own A/B runs.

_comment: Motherboard chipset packages. SEPARATE from the gaming GPU blocks above and read by a
different code path (DriverIntelligence.EvaluateChipset), because nothing here is the
same shape as a GPU family:
- AMD ships ONE package for every socket. The revision on the X870E page is the same
revision offered for B650, X570, B450 and Threadripper, so there is one entry here
and not one per socket. Verified 2026-09-25 against AMD's own X870E download page,
whose support list runs from A320 through WRX90 at a single revision number.
- There is no `recommended`, no `latest_tested` and no `avoid`. Nobody has benched a
chipset package, so the card is INFORMATIONAL: it states the installed revision and
the published one and stops there. It must never tell anyone to install something,
which is the same default-is-Hold posture the GPU engine takes for measured reasons.
Adding a `recommended` key here would be claiming evidence that does not exist.
- `installed` comes from the uninstall registry, NOT from PnP driver versions. The
per-device versions the package installs (GPIO2, I2C, PSP, PPM) each carry their own
unrelated numbers and none of them equals the package revision.
latest_known / latest_known_released / latest_known_reports carry the same meaning as in
the GPU blocks. Since 2026-10-03 the weekly driver watch owns these three fields too,
read from AMD's own chipset download page; everything else in this block stays human-owned.
SOURCING WARNING: read the vendor page, never a search summary. On 2026-09-25 a search
summary reported the current AMD package as 8.02.18.557 from March; the vendor page said
8.08.12.551 from August, two releases and five months newer.

amd.latest_known_reports: AMD lists one itself: the Ryzen provisioning package occasionally fails to install or upgrade. Nothing has been reported against it in the field yet.
